memory_candidates.content: When a deploy loader entry in manifest.json provides.<category> resolves to a directory (entry_kind 'dir' or 'file_or_dir'), the deploy copies it recursively (see lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/loader.lua's scan_directory_recursive branches). A new file placed inside an already-registered directory entry (e.g. a new file under context/contracts/ when 'contracts' is already listed) deploys automatically WITHOUT needing its own manifest.json entry -- only genuinely new top-level provides entries (a new script, a new top-level context file, a new directory itself) need registration. Verify this against the target category's entry_kind before assuming a new file needs a manifest edit.

deploy-root-guard.sh (sourced by scripts/*.sh to reject source-store invocation) is depth-specific to one level under .claude/ or .opencode/ (scripts/). It uses BASH_SOURCE[0], which inside a sourced file resolves to the ORIGINAL calling script's path, not the guard's own path -- so a script living two levels deep (scripts/lint/*.sh, scripts/tests/*.sh) would have its parent-directory check strip to '.claude/scripts' rather than '.claude', never matching the guard's case pattern, and would incorrectly reject even a validly deployed invocation. Scripts at that depth needing source-store-invocation support (REPO_ROOT env override for direct agent-system/extensions/... execution) should NOT reuse deploy-root-guard.sh unmodified; use `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` instead for read-only lints (safe, since there's no destructive-write risk to mask), falling back to a REPO_ROOT override then a script-relative default.

allowed-tools: and mcp-servers: (hyphenated) are NOT valid Claude Code subagent frontmatter fields -- they are silently ignored (not rejected), which lets the drift go unnoticed indefinitely. allowed-tools: is a SKILL.md/slash-command field; the subagent equivalent is tools: (comma-separated string allowlist). mcp-servers: is a misspelling of the real camelCase mcpServers: field. An agent carrying allowed-tools: runs with UNRESTRICTED inherited tool access despite appearing to declare a restriction -- correcting it to tools: is a real behavior change (narrows access), not a cosmetic rename, and should be preceded by a tool-scope audit of the agent's actual body + dispatching skill before applying the fix.
